name: @playform/hook-dsh-tool-coach
description: The tool-coach hook: a DeepSeek Harness plugin that teaches the model to stop using the terminal for file content. It hooks the tools/post- and tools/pre-execute waterfalls, the agent/pre-step boundary, the system-prompt/assemble waterfall and the tools/change notification, and runs a four-tier coaching ladder over TERMINAL tool calls (bash, pwsh by default): tier 0 writes a durable ledger line for every detected content-class offense; tier 1 prepends a labeled tools/post-execute additionalContexts notice (source {kind: 'tool-coach', form: 'notice', summary}) once a class accumulates the configured strikes within the sliding window, cooled down between notes; tier 2 escalates to a persistent system-prompt section (heading + three fixed rules + a live-fetched tool table capped at maxSectionTools rows) while the strikes last, auto-cleared after a clean window; tier 3 (opt-in, enforce) denies the terminal call through tools/pre-execute with the model-facing reason text. Detection is deliberately adversarial: command normalization (quote layers, $IFS, $VAR/${VAR} to markers, $(...) and backticks to subshells, heredoc bodies stripped), a class-determining intent-marker scan, a craft library for obfuscated variants, and a catch-all that lands any write-intent marker on a real path - so novel zero-day forms still count. The dedicated tools are never judged; every note names the correct tool with its LIVE registry description (fetched via ctx.tools.schemas(), first sentence, key parameter) and falls back to a static table on any fetch failure. Plan: Documentation/Plans/TOOL-COACH-OPERATIVE-PLAN.md (Part 3) + TOOL-COACH-PLAN.md + TOOL-COACH-RESEARCH.md.
